stances_toward.note: Partner, not ally: no treaty is signed. The Vuvale Partnership was elevated in July 2025 (Albanese and Rabuka), with treaty negotiations due to start at the Defence Ministers' Meeting in Suva on 3 Oct 2025; a security agreement is in drafting and Fiji is posting police and defence attaches to Canberra. The 2025-29 development package is reported at about A$500m, with AFP officers working inside the Fiji police and A$12m for container screening at Lautoka and Suva. Warming because each step is larger than the last. Bond - affinity: shared Pacific and Commonwealth ties, not kinship. The 'friends to all' line (ASPI) is the reason this is not an alliance.

stances_toward.note: Partner with a grievance. Australia's bugging of Dili's cabinet during the 2004 Timor Sea talks (the Witness K case, alleged) has not been apologised for: the charges against Bernard Collaery were dropped in July 2022, which Dili welcomed, but Canberra has not admitted the operation and no 2025 apology was found (HRLC, Jan 2024). The Albanese visit of 28-29 Jan 2026 produced a joint declaration, 'a new partnership for a new era': US$220m for human development, US$80m for private-sector development, US$8.2m for ASEAN and WTO participation, a 10% share of combined future upstream Greater Sunrise revenue to a Timor-Leste infrastructure fund (other reporting gives a larger share; not resolved here), and 10,000 Timorese workers in Australia by 2027-28. The friction is the field: Dili wants a pipeline to its south coast, Woodside prefers Darwin, and first gas has slipped to 2034-35. Grade partner rather than reluctant partner because the cooperation is broad and no source calls it grudging; trend stable because the declaration and the slipping gas talks pull in opposite directions.
